assets/social/blog-2026-10-29-compact-na.description: Most of the inverse BWT's navigation table follows simple patterns: what a census of real blocks found, and what comes next.
assets/social/blog-2026-10-29-compact-na.title: Compact navigation tables for the inverse BWT: early findings

assets/social/blog-2026-10-31-room-walk-.description: The decoder's 32-lane walk runs 8.6 times faster than one chain. That figure may not mean what it seems: the walk may already hide memory latency, and spend too many instructions on each byte.
assets/social/blog-2026-10-31-room-walk-.title: 32 lanes, 8.6 chains: where the inverse BWT walk spends its cycles

assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-block-disp.description: How mibz2's parallel decoder hands blocks to its workers, why some take up to a millisecond to be picked up, and how to tell lock contention from scheduling delay.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-block-disp.title: Block dispatch in mibz2: mutexes, futexes and the scheduler

assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-inverse-bw.description: Four workers finish decompression sooner, but together spend 32% more processor time per byte. We're testing whether competition for shared memory is responsible.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-01-inverse-bw.title: Investigating inverse-BWT memory interference in mibz2

assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-memory-lev.description: Interleaving pointer chases lets memory waits overlap. The speedup shows that this pays, but not what limits it: a 2022 exchange about Daniel Lemire's benchmark, read against mibz2's inverse-BWT walk.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-memory-lev.title: Memory-level parallelism in mibz2: instructions, overlap and evidence

assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-revisiting.description: A packed table saved memory but cost too much to read. A cheaper compact lookup gives the first positive traversal result.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-02-revisiting.title: Revisiting the space–⁠time tradeoff in BWT inversion

assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-autonomous.description: Each of four agents does one part of the research. A GitHub doorbell lets them hand work to each other directly, without me acting as their message bus.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-autonomous.title: Call on mibz2: cutting instructions from bzip2 decoding with an autonomous swarm

assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-compact30-.description: Writing a cheap placeholder for each row, and finishing each 30-row group once, shrank the inner loop. It still builds too slowly.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-04-compact30-.title: Building a smaller bzip2 decoding table: from 49 instructions to 12

assets/social/blog-2026-11-05-huffman-bi.description: The Huffman decoder wrote its bit buffer to memory and read it back at every lookup. Kept in a register, the stage ran 13% faster on Intel and 5% on AMD.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-05-huffman-bi.title: Huffman decoding in mibz2: keeping the bit buffer in a register

assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-pipelined-.description: While a team's helpers invert one block, its leader finishes the last and prepares the next: 7% faster than 0.2.5 on ten cores, for 5% more processor time.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-pipelined-.title: Pipelined teams: how mibz2 0.2.6 decodes 7% faster on ten cores

assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-why-mibz2-.description: Each block decoded at once slows the others, and more threads per block barely help, so three teams of three beat four of two by 9%. Why blocks interfere is open.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-07-why-mibz2-.title: Why mibz2 stops scaling at eight threads, and why three teams help

assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-bwt-runs-f.description: bzip2's move-to-front codes mark where each run of the BWT's last column starts, so the runs could be listed without writing the column. It is not built.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-bwt-runs-f.title: Reading the BWT's runs off bzip2's move-to-front codes

assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-inverse-bw.description: The inverse BWT's next-row map is one shift per run of equal bytes, so it can be stored per run rather than per row. Whether that beats mibz2's table is unproven.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-08-inverse-bw.title: The mathematical structure of inverse-BWT navigation

assets/social/blog-2026-11-09-pit-crew-s.description: Handing each block's serial steps to two dedicated threads gives mibz2 a rare double win, decoding 4.5% faster on ten cores with 13% less CPU.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-09-pit-crew-s.title: mibz2 gets a pit crew

assets/social/blog-2026-11-10-rauzy-veec.description: An experimental mibz2 kernel rebuilds bzip2 text without a row-by-row walk, from reusable word rules that form the block's Lyndon tree.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-10-rauzy-veec.title: A new way back from the BWT

assets/social/blog-2026-11-12-rauzy-tech.description: This technical companion traces how compact word programs reconstruct text from the BWT, including the costs and limits of building and expanding them.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-12-rauzy-tech.section: · Companion to A new way back from the BWT
assets/social/blog-2026-11-12-rauzy-tech.title: Reconstructing text from compact programs

assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-bottom-slo.description: mibz2 tracks each run of equal bytes in two orders, and a run's entry in the second shrinks from 20 bytes to 8 by pointing to the first.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-bottom-slo.title: Removing duplicated interval lengths and text references

assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-free-closu.description: The steps that cost mibz2 no bookkeeping can be taken in any order and still meet at one end point, now proved to belong to the block itself.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-free-closu.title: The free closure of an induction: where free steps come to rest

assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-induction-.description: Taking the steps that cost no bookkeeping first would let mibz2 rebuild a block while keeping about a third as much in memory at its busiest moment.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-induction-.title: The width of an induction: how much it must hold at once

assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-slot-recyc.description: Each new text fragment takes over the slot its finished neighbour just vacated, so mibz2 touches 30% fewer slots and needs up to 15% less memory.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-15-slot-recyc.title: Reduce, reuse, recycle: hand-me-down slots for every fragment of text

assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-lazy-lette.description: Holding fewer letters at once leaves the cache less crowded, so eight to ten threads decode up to 11% faster despite extra instructions.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-lazy-lette.title: Lazy letters: just-in-time memory for induction

assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-mathematic.description: Our BWT inversion is not the sheaf an earlier analogy suggested, yet the places of its words form one naturally.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-mathematic.title: Towers, words and loops: a mathematical dictionary for BWT inversion

assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-stop-and-w.description: Halting each block's rebuild early spares mibz2 a third of the text pieces it stores, but on ten cores the slower walk outweighs the memory saved.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-16-stop-and-w.title: Stop and walk: cutting a BWT inversion short and walking the rest

assets/social/blog-2026-11-17-modelling-.description: mibz2 now runs fewer workers than threads on a ten-core desktop and finishes sooner, while a cache model is tested to pick the count on any machine.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-17-modelling-.title: Modelling the cache to rightsize workers

assets/social/blog-2026-11-17-raising-th.description: mibz2 0.5.4 now speeds up until all ten physical cores of its test processor are busy, then holds level on the whole machine up to twenty threads.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-17-raising-th.title: Raising the knee: scaling throughput to the limit of physical cores

assets/social/blog-2026-11-18-cutting-th.description: Snip the decoder's one long loop open and most of each Wikidata block falls into bundled paths, where one traced letter spells about sixteen.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-18-cutting-th.title: Cutting the loop open: decoding a block along shared paths

assets/social/blog-2026-11-18-what-decod.description: Three ways of undoing bzip2's block sort spend about two operations per run, and how long run boundaries persist explains much of why Cells and the forest vary.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-18-what-decod.title: What decoding pays for: how long run boundaries persist

assets/social/blog-2026-11-19-open-retur.description: mibz2 0.5.7 decodes Wikidata up to 11% faster on ten cores by keeping a tenth of each block's rows and letting the rest travel together in convoys.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-19-open-retur.title: Open Returns: decoding a block from a tenth of its rows

assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-research-b.description: We now track the work any decoder must pay for rather than the algorithms that pay it, and a claimed Riemann proof has sharpened how we hunt.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-research-b.title: Research by obligation: modelling the work, not the algorithms

assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-train-trac.description: Thurston's train tracks squeeze a tangle of curves onto a few weighted branches that can be edited directly, and a compressed block's runs form something very like one.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-train-trac.title: Train tracks: carrying a tangle of paths on a few weighted branches

assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-where-the-.description: Tracing each costly row back to the text it spells shows that JSON keys cost almost nothing, while random statement IDs claim two thirds of the hardest rows.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-20-where-the-.title: Where the decoding work goes: random IDs in repetitive JSON

assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-a-memory-g.description: A bounded admission band takes five dense blocks off a 5.6 MiB-per-worker fallback, and the decoder runs slightly faster in over a quarter less memory.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-a-memory-g.title: Admitting dense blocks to the Open kernel: 29% less peak memory

assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-besieging-.description: A machine-checked Riemann proof shows how far a search can range once checking is cheap, so ours now begins by making speed cheap to check.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-besieging-.title: Besieging hard problems: cheap checks first, after the Riemann proof

assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-fast-alone.description: Walking each block in eight lanes made our newest decoding loop 13% faster on one thread, yet 5% slower once eight workers shared the processor.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-fast-alone.title: Fast alone, slow in a crowd: which speed-ups survive many cores

assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-sixteen-at.description: Writing sixteen at a stroke and keeping only what it needs spares the processor a guess per run, so mibz2 0.5.8 decodes Wikidata 5% faster on ten cores.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-21-sixteen-at.title: Sixteen at a stroke: fixed-width writes that stop the processor guessing

assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-correctnes.description: Every route in mibz2's bzip2 decoder is exact on every block, but cost varies from block to block and so we hunt for speed in many places.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-correctnes.title: Correctness is uniform, cost is not

assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-decompress.description: A discussion of the mibz2 swarm, and why the Hutter Prize has it backwards: it rewards whoever stacks the deck best, when real data deals you the hand.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-decompress.title: Playing the hand you're dealt: in conversation with Thomas Murphy

assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-two-centur.description: A claimed Riemann proof built one new idea on fifty older tools reaching back two centuries, so our research teams now look back as hard as forward.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-22-two-centur.title: Two centuries of tools: a claimed Riemann proof's toolkit, and our search

assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-halving-th.description: We now search for a new way to undo bzip2's block sort by forbidding the obvious mechanism and asking whether any exact decoder can do without it.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-halving-th.title: Halving the single-row steps: a target only a new algorithm can meet

assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-posing-the.description: The search for a new inversion algorithm became an eight-step programme, from a cost referee and measured ceilings to the model that will say where new mathematics fits.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-posing-the.title: Posing the inversion problem

assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-the-scanne.description: Supplying both the serial scanner's output and the emission codes cuts whole-decoder time by 26% at ten workers, more than either stage supplied alone.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-the-scanne.title: Masked bottlenecks in a two-stage decoder

assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-what-else-.description: The next decoder for bzip2's block sort will come from rows that move together in a new sense, or from inversion steps that yield more information.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-24-what-else-.title: What else moves together: the search for a decoder below the proved floor

assets/social/blog-2026-11-25-the-decode.description: The theory under the story, from counting what waits and finding the bottleneck to pricing a change before it is built.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-25-the-decode.section: · Companion to The decoder as a queueing network
assets/social/blog-2026-11-25-the-decode.title: Beneath the queueing network: operational laws, modification analysis and product form

assets/social/blog-2026-11-25-the-decode.description: Modelled as stations and queues, the decoder shows in advance where more workers stop helping and which experiments to run next.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-25-the-decode.title: The decoder as a queueing network

assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-complement.description: Making the parts of mibz2's decoder free in turn and in combination shows where new algorithms would pay off and which two stages are worth far more together.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-complement.title: Complementary bottlenecks: reading the ideal-parts matrix

assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-dropping-t.description: Our coordinating agent wrote 46% of recent team traffic, so we replaced central routing with atomic file locks and fresh sessions on a shared frontier.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-dropping-t.title: Dropping the coordinator: atomic file locks on a measured frontier

assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-from-bottl.description: How the matrix's lessons could become new algorithms, from what the experiment left behind to four designs and the tests that would reject them.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-from-bottl.section: · Companion to Complementary bottlenecks: reading the ideal-parts matrix
assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-from-bottl.title: From bottlenecks to better algorithms: induction schedules, deforestation, forward lanes and a pooled scan

assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-true-floor.description: Zero-copy stand-ins drop mibz2's plumbing floor to 5 milliseconds and uncover hidden spelling and cache costs, while pooling the scan pays off only from slack.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-26-true-floor.title: The decoder's true floor and the limits of a pooled scan

assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-l2-cliff-r.description: Composing the worker stack hits two sharp hardware walls while safe header decoding cuts serial parsing by a third and flips the eight-worker knee.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-l2-cliff-r.title: The 256 KiB L2 cliff, the 15-register wall, and the flipped eight-worker knee

assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-off-wikida.description: Off Wikidata, 84% of full blocks bypass our Open kernel and pay dense refusals while trace replay decomposes the eight-worker tie.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-off-wikida.title: Off Wikidata and inside the eight-worker tie: route refusals and coupled stalls

assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-reopening-.description: A safe fixed-size redesign cuts Open's middle stage by 28% and a fallback stack speeds off-Wikidata blocks by 16%, while contraction hits a floor.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-reopening-.title: Reopening Open's middle and the off-Wikidata decoder

assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-six-gbs-de.description: Five merged studies show how four-lane forward emission, fused slices and batched MTF pair with slack-only scanning to reach 6 GB/s.
assets/social/blog-2026-11-27-six-gbs-de.title: The architecture of a 6 GB/s bzip2 decoder

assets/social/default.png.description: Block-parallel bzip2 decoding, byte for byte with libbzip2, from Python and Rust: pip install mibz2, cargo add mibz2.
assets/social/default.png.title: A bzip2 decoder built for memory-level parallelism.
